## PM · review of PR #5572 — the ablation is the right one for a type-level fix

Most reverse verifications this session mutated behaviour and watched tests go red. That would have proved nothing here, because the renderer **already** resolved locale maps at runtime — `pickLocalized` takes `unknown`, so every vitest assertion is green with the narrow declaration too. You ablated the thing that actually carries the fix:

> reverted only the type declaration to `label?: string` (source-only, confirmed on disk via grep), reran `type-check` → **exit 2**, TS2322 at exactly the new test's locale-map literal (`record-alert.test.tsx:219:17`, "Type '{ en: string; zh-CN: string; }' is not assignable to type 'string'"); the pre-existing plain-string CTA test stayed **unaffected**. Restored, re-ran → exit 0.

That establishes two separate things, and the second is the one reviewers usually skip: not just *that* the pin fails without the fix, but *which* test carries the discrimination — the new locale-map case, not the plain-string case sitting three lines above it. I had flagged exactly this doubt on my own read before your report arrived; you had already closed it.

### Checked independently, not taken from the report

- **Both copies widened** — `schema.properties.action.label` (:98) and the flat compat mirror `schema.action.label` (:108). Finding one and shipping was this card's failure mode; triage said "both copies" for that reason.
- **The stale docblock was rewritten, not left to rot.** It previously read *"deliberately NOT widened here (objectui#4998)"* — a sentence that would have become false the moment this merged. It now states the widening, why (`pickLocalized` parity with `title`/`body`), and that it is type-only.
- **The out-of-scope half stayed out.** The published surface still declares `action` as a bare `object` with the member shape in prose, so there is no manifest arm to align; parked on #3795 and said so in *both* the code comment and the changeset, which is where a future reader will actually look.
- **Unprompted care worth naming:** wrapping the new case in a real `I18nProvider` pinned to `en` so it does not ride whatever language another test file left on the global i18next singleton. Nothing asked for that; a locale test that silently depends on file execution order is a flake waiting for a busy CI runner.

This was dispatched at the **sonnet floor** — triage measured it S-mechanical with a landed precedent (#4970) and correctness decided by `type-check` rather than judgment. That call holds: the floor was the right tier, and the work came back with a better ablation than the tier required.

CI on #5572: `Build & E2E`, `Build Docs` and all three changeset gates green; the four `Test` shards and **`Type Check`** still `in_progress`, nothing red. `Type Check` is the gate that decides this card, so no verdict and no enqueue until it reads `completed: success` by name.
